summary: All 11 findings confirmed in substance; none refuted. No file was removed: nothing was found that makes a downloaded file unusable for the stated purpose (test material and listening); the NASA speech files, including the two ISS files with a named current NASA astronaut, are now marked per file as test material that must not ship. Fixed in tools/audio/fetch.py, assets/audio/downloads.json, assets/audio/selection.json and a regenerated assets/audio/CREDITS.md; new tools/audio/tests/test_fetch.py (27 tests). Plugin findings need the fixes written below (not edited, other agent's file). VERIFIED this session: fetch.py --check (57 entries, 0 problems) and the unit tests (27 OK, run with -I -m unittest discover -s tools/audio/tests); old fetch.py (commit 4a0ea2d) reproduces findings 4, 5, 7 and the new code refuses them; NASA guidelines page re-read with curl and compared; Kenney License.txt of all five packs read; ISS API record read (no credit or rights field); JSON.stringify amplification measured in node (6002 bytes to 2009002 bytes). NOT VERIFIED: Vite's CORS and host-check behaviour (finding 8, taken from the reviewer, not run), a real full disk, a real redirect from a NASA host, a real download run (nothing was downloaded: all 57 entries were already complete), the speech marks (inferred from titles and pages, nobody listened). Note: the Licence column still says 'Public domain (NASA)'; the commercial limits are in the terms, evidence and Notes column, not in that label.
plugin_fix_for_auditionPlugin_ts: Findings audition-trusts-vite-defaults and audition-put-amplification are confirmed by reading the plugin: it has no Origin, Host, Sec-Fetch-Site or Content-Type check, and it writes JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2) in place with no size cap.

1. At the top of the /audio-lib handler, after the pathname checks, add: const origin = req.headers.origin; const site = req.headers['sec-fetch-site']; if ((origin !== undefined && origin !== `http://${req.headers.host}`) || (typeof site === 'string' && site !== 'same-origin' && site !== 'none')) { send(res, 403, 'cross-origin request refused'); return; }  (the audition page is served by the same Vite server, so its own requests are same-origin and still pass; another local web app on another port is refused for reads and writes).

2. In the PUT /ratings branch, before readBody: if (!String(req.headers['content-type'] ?? '').toLowerCase().startsWith('application/json')) { send(res, 415, 'content type must be application/json'); return; }  (packages/client/src/dev/audition/ratings.ts already sends application/json).

3. Replace the write: const text = JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2) + '\n'; if (Buffer.byteLength(text) > 2 * MAX_BODY) { send(res, 413, 'ratings larger than 2 MB once written'); return; } const tmp = ratingsFile + '.' + process.pid + '.tmp'; await fs.writeFile(tmp, text, 'utf-8'); await fs.rename(tmp, ratingsFile);  (caps the 330x expansion and makes the replacement atomic).
4. In readBody, when size exceeds MAX_BODY call req.destroy() after the 413 has been sent, or answer 413 from the Content-Length header first, so an endless stream is not read forever (not tested).
